# Incoming corridor observations

The unchanged source, repeated source, and bundled JAR produced identical ordinary and diagnostic TSV files.
Five compiled helper classes also matched.
The artifacts remain private until independent review and lead adoption.

The ordinary fixture contains nine cases, 54 snapshots, 45 actual calls, and ten identity discoveries.
It records 96 actor views and 48 incoming-corridor views.
The diagnostic fixture contains two cases, five snapshots, and three actual calls.

Ordinary cases use a real paused MainWindow, VisibleWorld, InfoToolbar, World, GeneticCode, and Organism.
The helper cancels the real timer before capture.
Where actors exist, a real pasted selected sentinel prevents the null-parent selection callback during arrivals.
Both queue reception and frame processing use original InCorridor methods.
World.time processes real arrivals before tree insertion and movement.

The ordinary cases cover these outcomes:

- Construct one actor before explicit paste, retaining its orientation draw and uninitialized arrays.
- Process empty incoming queues without creating candidates.
- Consume a null queue entry before the next code.
- Block one EYE candidate repeatedly while retaining its actual identity and vision classifications.
- Release that candidate, then process shared-code and cloned-code FIFO entries independently.
- Retry an outside-world candidate while preserving alternating signed-zero velocity responses.
- Retain origin-death effects through another failed retry and a later successful paste.
- Process two incoming corridors against live earlier arrivals before indexing.
- Move and index a successful arrival during the same World.time call.
- Recheck a forward first branch on the same retained candidate after an explicit input repair.

The diagnostic empty genome constructs successfully and pastes successfully at 3500,3500.
That direct paste does not call World.addOrganism.
The zero-span corridor constructor throws IllegalArgumentException before candidate construction.
These observations remain compatibility obligations, including the successful empty-genome behavior.
They are not user-approved exclusions or evidence that Rust rejects them correctly.

Initial recipes use only supplied G/N input blocks.
g0 and g1 are explicit recipes; g2 supplies the sentinel; g3 supplies another explicit code.
g4 uses the actual GeneticCode clone of g0.
All later G/N rows are observations.
Queue entries retain actual GeneticCode identities, including duplicate references and null.
Numeric organism IDs never define actor identity.

The helper reuses the frozen frame protocol and these additions:

| Row or operation | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| F stage corridor field type value | Observe seven actual incoming fields, including inherited ownership and bounds |
| D stage arrivalN id genome | Discover an actual new member or retained incoming candidate by object identity |
| K stage corridor.new corridor ~ | Call the real InCorridor constructor |
| K stage corridor.receive corridor genome-or-~ | Call receiveOrganism with the exact supplied reference |
| K stage corridor.frame corridor ~ | Call one real incoming frame |
| K stage construct actor genome | Call the real deferred Organism constructor |
| K stage paste actor x,y | Call real pasteOrganism with supplied integer coordinates |
| B stage paste boolean | Record the actual paste return value |
| K stage time victim ~ | Call one real World.time |
| X stage class message | Record an actual diagnostic exception; encode its UTF8 message with Base64 |

F contains _reference, bounds, pendingOrganisms, nextOrganism, world, travellingOrganism, and connection.
Observe InCorridor and Organism identities before Rectangle values.
Empty queues use an empty value; null entries use ~.
Retain discovered actors after success, removal, or candidate release.
J observes stored envelopes without rebuilding the tree.
Emit J in retained actor registration order; Q records actual query result order.
Q uses the real JTS query API and can build its internal index.

Explicit I controls install incoming registry references and the corridor-existence flag.
This controlled setup excludes the separate World.addCorridors pair API.
Other additions set corridor bounds and a supplied gene branch.
Every changed value appears before its affected source call.
No expected actor, endpoint, geometry, gas, or statistics output supplies a constructor input.

The ordinary fixed ledger has 46,662 rows:

| Bucket | Rows |
| --- | ---: |
| Schema-eligible derived observations | 41,295 |
| Supplied G/N constructor inputs | 3,140 |
| Explicit collaborator observations | 396 |
| Other inputs, schemas, commands, and metadata | 1,831 |

The 396 collaborator rows contain 192 O ownership/UI rows, 108 V UI/outgoing rows, and 96 F outgoing/connection rows.
F.world and V.worldStatistics use explicit logical owner projections.
This projection preserves ownership without requiring Java object layout in Rust.
Every other ordinary observation remains eligible for exact comparison under the established geometry contract.

The diagnostic ledger has 3,833 rows.
It contains 2,866 eligible observations, 600 supplied G/N rows, 20 collaborator rows, and 347 other rows.
Keep its actual outcomes separate until the corresponding compatibility corrections pass.

Only _m, _m1, _m2, _mass, and _I retain the existing geometry allowance.
That allowance is 1e-10 multiplied by max(1,abs(expected)), with established finite, NaN, and infinity handling.
All other floats, RNG suffixes, colors, endpoints, bounds, aliases, order, gases, and statistics remain exact.
R consumes only a serialized Random copy.
Serialization can canonicalize a cached NaN payload; this helper does not exercise Gaussian draws.

The driver preserved 74 original hash/size/mode pins, 159 source classes, and 576 prior fixture files.
It verified six failing isolation guards before accepting native capture.
Four compile commands and nine native commands have same-controller owned-group readbacks.
All nine native groups were absent after bounded cleanup.
The capture also verified its owned root group.
These checks do not establish full-host process absence or observed network traffic.

Remaining gates include independent producer review, Rust differential replay, outgoing transfer, transport, concurrency, and connection lifecycle.
Player controls, full UI parity, rendering, hardware performance, and complete network compatibility remain separate gates.
No production Rust file, canonical fixture, tracker, instruction, or global configuration changed here.
